The correct value is 7, which none of the three solutions gives, so I am choosing the closest one.

**Derivation.** The recurrence gives tan(a_{n+1}) = sin(a_n), so sin(a_{n+1}) = sin(a_n)·cos(a_{n+1}). Hence cos(a_{n+1}) = sin(a_{n+1})/sin(a_n).

Telescoping, cos(a_2)···cos(a_16) = sin(a_16)/sin(a_1).

Let s_n = sin²(a_n). From tan²(a_{n+1}) = s_n we get s_{n+1} = s_n/(1+s_n), so 1/s_{n+1} = 1/s_n + 1.

Since 1/s_1 = 4/3, we have 1/s_16 = 4/3 + 15 = 49/3. So sin(a_16) = √3/7.

The product is then cos(a_1) · sin(a_16)/sin(a_1) = (1/2)·(√3/7)/(√3/2) = 1/7, and its reciprocal is 7.

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 has the correct telescoping setup but takes sin(a_16) = √3/64 with no justification. The true value is √3/7, so 64 is wrong.
- Solution 2 gets 7√2 from invented cosine values and a made-up telescoping, so it is wrong.
- Solution 3 telescopes to sin(a_17)/sin(a_1), which includes cos(a_17) rather than cos(a_1), and its value of a_17 is also wrong, so √13 is wrong.

I picked Solution 2 because its answer, 7√2, is the closest to 7.

CHOICE: 2
